bullets: Macro forecasting is mostly humility plus a few dependable signals—reliability of data trumps cleverness of model.
The reliability of data determines the quality of forecasts, not the sophistication of the model used.
Framing matters because it reveals the trade-offs inherent in any forecasting decision.
Teams using BloombergNEF have demonstrated that consistent, dependable signals outperform complex models over time.
The second-order effect is often missed: reliable data enables better risk management across economic scenarios.
Reliability of data trumps cleverness of model—this framing exposes the real trade-offs being made.
Running a concept for two weeks enables iteration and reveals whether it holds in practice.
The key insight is not just what you forecast, but how you choose to trust the data.
